defects.title: GET /permission/{permissionId} answers 404 for an EXISTING approval row: the documented 200 is unreachable

evidence.request: GET /permission/t1-perm-0002   (approval_requests row t1-perm-0002 injected into the scratch DB, status=pending)

control.note: the same row read through the consensus route returns the documented 200, so the row is readable and the shim handler is the failing surface.

evidence.root_cause: internal/shim/opencode/server.go:2235 getPermission SELECTs ar.sql_preview, ar.decision_reason and ar.resolved_at; the shipped SQLite schema approval_requests (migrations/001_initial_schema.sql) has target_sql, review_notes and reviewed_at instead. The query error is swallowed into a 404, so a schema bug is reported as 'not found'.

defects.class_: status-code contract violation, silently masked as not-found
defects.prior_candidate_recheck: NEW (derived from the same root cause as T1-D5)

defects.title: POST /permission/{permissionId}/resolve returns 500 on a well-formed body

evidence.response_body: {"error":{"code":"INTERNAL_ERROR","message":"failed to resolve permission: sqlite: exec: SQL logic error: no such column: decision_reason (1)"}}
evidence.expected: one of 200|400|401|404 — 500 is not in the documented set

control.note: the consensus route POST /api/v1/approvals/{id}/review resolves the same row with the documented 200.

evidence.root_cause: internal/shim/opencode/server.go:2278 UPDATE approval_requests SET status=$1, decision_reason=$2, resolved_at=$3, resolved_by='opencode-shim' — those three columns do not exist in the shipped approval_requests schema (review_notes / reviewed_at / reviewer_id are the real columns). SQLite raises 'no such column: decision_reason', surfaced verbatim as a 500.
evidence.probe_methodology_note: The bulk sweep's minimal `{}` body is refused by the decision vocabulary check (400) BEFORE the UPDATE runs, which masks the defect. It only reproduces with a well-formed {'decision': 'approved'|'rejected'|'modified'} body.

defects.prior_candidate_recheck: CONFIRMED (was listed as an unverified claim of 500 vs {200,400,401,404})

schema_format_findings.title: heartbeat_at is not RFC 3339 on GET /api/v1/sessions/{sessionId}

evidence.note: the SAME field on the SAME resource is serialised two different ways depending on the handler: space-separated on GET, RFC 3339 on PATCH. `date-time` requires RFC 3339.

schema_format_findings.title: GET /api/v1/approvals/{approvalId} returns created_at as the zero time

evidence.note: the stored value is present and non-null; the read path drops it to 0001-01-01T00:00:00Z.

schema_format_findings.title: POST /api/v1/approvals/{approvalId}/review writes a non-parseable reviewed_at (Go time.String with the monotonic reading)

evidence.db_value: 2026-09-30 03:14:27.257223769 -0500 -05 m=+179.071315254  (SELECT reviewed_at FROM approval_requests WHERE id='t1-perm-0002')
evidence.note: reviewed_at is written with Go's time.Time.String(), including the 'm=+…' monotonic suffix. It is not RFC 3339 and is not parseable by the declared date-time format.

observations.title: 8 operations answer 2xx without any credential
observations.note: health/doc/global/health/mcp declare `security: []` and are intentionally public. The four /instance operations inherit the document-level BearerAuth[] requirement yet serve 2xx with no credential — a posture question for security review, not a status-code mismatch.

observations.title: POST /mcp rejects Bearer auth and demands an MCP-specific credential channel

evidence.response_body: {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"error":{"code":-32000,"message":"Authentication required","data":"API key missing from the MCP initialize request — provide it via --api-key or CONSENSUS_API_KEY (the MCP client forwards it in _meta.authorization)"}}

observations.note: the spec declares document-level `BearerAuth` (so the operation lists 401 among its documented statuses), but a Bearer header is refused: the JSON-RPC error answers -32000 'API key missing from the MCP initialize request — provide it via --api-key or CONSENSUS_API_KEY (the MCP client forwards it in _meta.authorization)'. A generic OpenAPI client (e.g. muster, which drives services from their own spec) cannot authenticate against /mcp using the declared scheme.

observations.title: POST /permission//resolve (empty path parameter) answers 307, not 4xx
observations.note: chi's redirect for a trailing/empty segment. Harmless, recorded for completeness: the sweep records it as INFO because the concrete URL is not a declared operation.
